title: Mini printf
story:
The translator's own print routine burned out. Build a replacement **without using printf** inside it: only `putchar`.

Write `int mini_printf(const char *fmt, ...)`. It understands `%d` (int), `%s` (string), `%c` (char), `%x` (an `unsigned int` in lowercase hex, like `ff`) and `%%`, prints every other character as it is, and **returns how many characters it printed**.

`main` is written for you. It reads a whole number `n` (any `int`, including the most negative one) and a word, makes three calls and prints what each returned.

Example: input `255 sos` prints
`n=255 w=sos`
`hex ff, first s, 100%`
`[sos|127]`
`12 22 10`

tests.expected:
n=255 w=sos
hex ff, first s, 100%
[sos|127]
12 22 10

n=-1 w=neg
hex ffffffff, first n, 100%
[neg|0]
11 28 8

n=-7 w=x
hex fffffff9, first x, 100%
[x|-3]
9 28 7

hints: Structure: walk `fmt`; plain characters go to `putchar` and add 1 to the count. On `%`, look at the next letter and call a helper. Make each helper **return** how many characters it printed.

To print a number without printf, peel digits off with `% 10` into a small char array, then print them backwards. Do the same with `% 16` and `"0123456789abcdef"` for hex. Don't forget that 0 has one digit.

`-n` overflows when n is -2147483648. Convert to a wider type first: `long long v = n; if (v < 0) { putchar('-'); v = -v; }`. For `%x`, read the argument as `unsigned int`, which makes -1 come out as `ffffffff`.
